Effect metadata MUST be a conservative superset of effects the function may perform; it MUST NOT omit a possible write, external effect or failure merely because an optimiser removed it in one build.
`sys.Table.assertions` MUST include every owner-scoped table assertion in source order and MUST expose the complete relation dependencies used for validation.
`sys.Assertion` MUST represent the contextual `assert` declarations specified by [assertions](#tables). A processor MUST NOT invent separate portable constraint/check/ensure/fact object kinds.
A table row count marked inexact MUST never be used as if it were an exact integrity fact.
Dependency traversal MUST be cycle-safe and deterministic.
A statically proven edge MUST use `exact` confidence. A conservative dynamic edge MAY use `possible`; tooling MUST NOT present `possible` as a proven call or write.
`sys.dependencies` and `sys.dependents` MUST preserve edge kind and source evidence rather than return only a set of names.
Diagnostic codes, primary spans and structured causes MUST remain available independently of a particular terminal or UI rendering.
Source paths returned outside explicitly trusted developer inspection MUST be repository-relative or redacted according to [redaction rules](#system-redaction).
Rendering a diagnostic MUST NOT mutate it, change its code or alter the underlying failure identity.

Secret values, decrypted source fragments, authorization material and unredacted connector payloads MUST NOT appear in diagnostic `message`, labels, causes, help, structured data, traces or presentation fallbacks.
A Git commit row and a semantic snapshot row MUST remain distinguishable even when they correspond one-to-one.
Hidden Orna refs MUST be visible through `sys.Ref.hidden` in explicit developer inspection and MUST remain valid ordinary Git refs.
A semantic diff MUST classify rename and rekey when identity evidence proves them; otherwise it MUST report conservative delete/add rather than invent identity.
Missing promisor objects MUST be represented explicitly. Introspection MUST NOT fabricate unavailable source, rows or statistics.
Storage locations and host paths are sensitive metadata and MUST follow the path-redaction rules.
`sys.Secret` MUST never expose decrypted secret bytes, derived authorization headers or a value formatter that reveals them.
A portable failure code MUST retain its meaning throughout the 1.x compatibility line.
Implementations MAY add structured fields and vendor causes, but MUST NOT replace a required portable primary code with a vendor-only code.
Failure messages may be localized; code, structured fields and causal identity remain stable.
Redaction MUST occur at the system-value boundary and MUST NOT depend solely on a renderer remembering to hide a value.
A redacted value MUST preserve safe type/identity metadata and an explicit redaction marker; it MUST NOT substitute plausible fake plaintext.
Canonical codecs MUST refuse to encode a protected value in reveal mode unless an explicitly trusted API outside generic `sys` grants that operation. No portable generic reveal API exists in 1.0.
Hashes of low-entropy secret values MUST be treated as sensitive. Domain separation alone does not make a dictionary-attackable hash safe; a public identifier MUST NOT reveal such a hash.
Explain output MUST be structured `sys.Plan` data. Human-readable tables or trees are `Present` renderings and are not the semantic result.
Actual execution counters MUST be absent when not measured; they MUST NOT be populated with estimates while marked actual.
A plan is snapshot-specific and MUST NOT be reused against a different schema revision without revalidation.
Every reflective `sys.invoke` or `sys.start` call MUST create an invocation identity before user code begins.
An unhandled ordinary failure MUST mark the invocation failed and roll back its Orna-controlled transaction before the failure is reported as terminal.
Cancellation MUST be recorded separately from ordinary failure and MUST bypass `|?` recovery inside the cancelled activation.
A run's `live` field is meaningful only for the current observation and MUST be false or absent in a purely historical projection.
Trace retention MAY be bounded, but the absence of discarded trace detail MUST be explicit and MUST NOT change invocation outcome.
Physical storage rows are introspection data and MUST NOT change the logical contents, ordering, equality or serialization of table rows.
A stored page MUST bind schema, logical key interval, generation and native object identity sufficiently to detect stale, overlapping or mismatched publication.
Missing lazily hydrated objects MUST be exposed as unavailable; a query may hydrate them according to policy but MUST NOT silently substitute incomplete results.
Build metadata MUST identify the complete source snapshot and compatibility coordinates used to produce an artifact.
A specification fixture listed as planned evidence MUST NOT be represented as passed unless an implementation actually executed it.
Every read/analysis function MUST return a normal typed value or relation that can be queried, encoded where supported and presented independently.
A root analysis function MUST NOT change checkout, refs, table contents, checkpoints, process state or retained failure state.
Name resolution and history functions MUST respect visibility and source redaction even in a trusted deployment.
`sys.Storage.profile` MUST identify the one recorded row profile; no new-format future-placement preference is exposed.
New-format admission MUST reject retired storage-preference functions rather than select a hidden legacy writer.
Physical maintenance MUST preserve every logical key/value, ordering and annotated Blob meaning; semantic row diff MUST be empty.
VFS path limits MUST be handled through reversible projection or explicit view errors, not by switching a table storage mode.
A maintenance stale-generation collision MUST preserve the prior authoritative root and report sys.storage.rewrite_conflict.
`sys.storage` is a grouping namespace, not a callable selector. Portable source MUST use `sys.Storage`, `sys.storage.objects` and the explicit `sys.admin` storage functions.
`sys.invoke` MUST NOT evaluate arbitrary source text or bypass the parser, resolver, type checker, visibility rules, effect rules or transaction model.
An argument envelope MUST NOT allow a value to masquerade as another static type merely because its data representation is compatible.

An idempotency key binds to function identity, exact revision, snapshot, expected result type, canonical typed arguments, invocation mode and relevant context. Reuse for a different tuple MUST fail with `sys.invoke.idempotency_mismatch`.
Returning a cached idempotent success is permitted only after the implementation proves the complete identity tuple matches and the retained result is valid under the same codec/type version.
`sys.start` MUST return a handle bound to one runtime generation and one invocation identity.
`sys.await` timeout MUST NOT cancel, detach, reparent or otherwise change the target invocation.
`sys.cancel` MUST be idempotent and MUST NOT convert cancellation into an ordinary recoverable failure inside the target.

Every type named by a portable `sys` field or function signature MUST be a language type, a core presentation/query type, a canonical system relation, an opaque identifier, a closed enum or a supporting value type enumerated by `api/sys.json`; undocumented pseudo-types are forbidden.

`sys.Value` MUST NOT be used as an implicit inference fallback or an implicit conversion route. It MUST preserve exact originating type identity and MUST require an explicit reflective API to unbox or validate it.
`sys.ArgumentMap` MUST reject duplicate names, preserve each argument's exact originating type and produce a deterministic canonical name order for idempotency hashing.

The typed `sys.invoke<T>` and `sys.start<T>` overloads MUST validate the function's declared result against the explicit `as: T` witness before any function effect occurs. A mismatch MUST fail with `sys.invoke.return_type`; no conversion chain is attempted.
`sys.InvocationResult<T>` MUST describe one complete terminal outcome and MUST satisfy the value/failure invariants stated above.
`sys.CheckpointPosition` MUST remain opaque outside its provider contract; generic code MUST NOT order it, increment it or synthesize a successor.
A conforming implementation MUST expose the supporting-type fields and invariants in `api/sys.json` and MUST reject a portable API claim whose type graph contains an unresolved name.
Direct mutation of a portable `sys` relation MUST fail at resolve/type-check time where statically evident and otherwise before any write is performed.
Every administrative function MUST define its transaction boundary, compare-and-set preconditions, failure codes and durable audit row.
An administrative function MUST validate all affected assertions before publishing its state transition.
A failed administrative operation MUST leave repository refs, logical CWD, checkpoints and runtime state at the last valid boundary described by its algorithm.
The 1.0 `sys.admin` boundary relies on OS/process isolation, Git/SSH credentials and the authenticated network perimeter; it MUST NOT be misrepresented as a built-in enterprise grants or role engine.
A continuation token MUST NOT be reused against a different snapshot, order, filter or redaction context.
Default iteration over an unordered system relation MUST NOT be documented as stable merely because one implementation happens to use object-ID order.
A multi-relation inspection operation requiring a coherent view MUST pin one observation snapshot/instant and expose it in the result.
A client that detects an observation-generation change during a live pagination sequence MUST restart or explicitly accept a new generation; rows MUST NOT be silently spliced across generations.
Retention policy MUST NOT delete data required to reproduce a committed logical snapshot while that snapshot remains advertised as complete.
Pruned optional detail MUST be represented as unavailable metadata, not as an empty value that could be mistaken for observed emptiness.
Retention and publication of runtime observations MUST never cause external effects or restart a program merely because a historical relation is queried.
A conformance claim MUST list every unavailable optional retention/detail profile but MUST NOT call a required portable member optional.
The conformance suite MUST test every root function with success, not-found/wrong-kind, snapshot, redaction and cancellation/failure cases applicable to that function.
The suite MUST verify that active valid examples use `sys.rt` and that `sys.runtime` appears only as an explicitly invalid name or diagnostic subject.
The suite MUST prove live handles fail across runtime generations and that snapshot references remain stable across CWD changes.
The suite MUST prove `sys.await` timeout leaves the target running and independently cancellable.
The suite MUST prove checkpoint compare-and-set, stream-write atomicity, failure retry/skip transitions and assertion validation under injected crashes and cancellation.
The suite MUST prove secret and path redaction before Inspect, Display, Present, codec and trace boundaries.

The suite MUST compare grouped handles with the same-snapshot canonical relations, applying the documented current-runtime/live filter to `sys.rt` handles rather than comparing them with all historical rows.
The suite MUST prove every canonical relation row exposes the correctly typed snapshot/runtime-pinned `reference`, including natural-key references that introduce no synthetic identity.
The suite MUST prove one row writer, annotation-aware semantic identity, physical-rewrite neutrality and stale-generation rejection across Orna and VFS edits.
The suite MUST verify [failure administration](#checkpoints), including stable delivery identity, versioned retries, skip, replay and resolve, and MUST reject system-row mutator methods.
The suite MUST test both `sys.source` and `sys.history` overloads with current, renamed, historical, missing, partially cloned and redacted files/objects.
The suite MUST exercise every snapshot-selector overload and prove that the returned `SnapshotRef` is pinned even when a named branch later moves.
The suite MUST exercise erased and typed invocation/start overloads, reject a mismatched `as: T` before effects, and prove `sys.Value` is never selected by ordinary failed inference.
The suite MUST validate every supporting value-type field, invariant and canonical encoding entry against `api/sys.json`.

Every administrative call MUST record an invocation with the function, safe arguments, owner, observed generation and terminal outcome. State-changing calls MUST retain an audit event in the same local transaction as their durable transition, or in the recoverable journal for a Git transition. A failed call records failure without claiming that its requested state change occurred.

Administrative operations MUST NOT run reentrantly inside an activation holding uncommitted table writes. Such a call fails with `sys.admin.busy`; the caller may finish its transaction and submit administration as a new activation. Read-only planning and verification may inspect a pinned generation without mutating it.

A state-changing command MUST expose one of: no admission, admitted and recoverable, or terminal. On reconnect, an unknown outcome MUST be inspected through its retained invocation/journal identity before another non-idempotent command is issued.
The REPL MUST use ordinary `use` syntax for namespace access and MUST NOT require a separate `:cd` namespace model.
`$_` and `$?` are REPL bindings and MUST NOT become implicit globals in module source.
Eager preview MUST NOT perform mutations, external I/O or other effects.
A relation preview MUST NOT require complete enumeration.
`:at` changes the default snapshot context for the session; it MUST NOT mutate repository HEAD.
`:watch` MUST use the same dependency and delta machinery as page sessions.
If Git already has the operation, Orna SHOULD preserve its name, flags and observable semantics. `orna mv` additionally preserves Orna semantic identity when the target is a definition or row key.
Runtime/checkpoint/failure detail and uncommon recovery operations SHOULD be available through typed `sys` values in the REPL and optional `std.devtools` pages.
`orna status --porcelain` MUST provide stable machine-readable output.
`orna status --short` SHOULD preserve Git's compact style while adding stable codes for runtime CWD summaries.
Errors MUST have stable codes, concise titles, source spans when available, causes and actionable help where known.
`orna explain <code>` SHOULD provide extended documentation.
Dynamic progress MUST be suppressed when output is not a terminal unless explicitly forced.
Terminal hyperlinks SHOULD be emitted when supported.
Normal CLI output, REPL output, diagnostics, generated user documentation and default frontend text MUST describe the problem and remedy using Orna concepts.

Normal user-facing output MUST NOT require the user to understand internal profile names, storage libraries, embedded-database terminology, wire encodings, object formats or extension ABI terminology.
`--verbose` MAY provide additional Orna-level context. Raw implementation details require `--debug` or an equivalent explicitly technical interface.
A diagnostic MUST lead with the user-visible condition and an actionable remedy. An implementation MAY attach machine-readable technical causes without rendering them by default.
`main.orna` MUST remain the fixed root module.
The reachable module graph MUST determine the database program; recursive filename scanning is not module admission.
Unreachable `.orna` files MUST NOT acquire declarations or execute because they exist.
Stored rows MUST belong to stable reachable table identities in the format-3 store; rows are not individually imported modules or executable scripts.
Published repositories MUST use ordinary Git objects, refs and commits readable by ordinary Git tooling.
The implementation MUST NOT substitute a proprietary history graph, LFS, or a separate mandatory media service.
A published commit MUST bind complete source/schema/data/content closure and exact dependency gitlinks; local availability and globally complete snapshot identity MUST be distinguished.
`HEAD` MUST exclude uncommitted runtime data.
Plain relation access MUST select CWD.
`relation.as_of(HEAD)` MUST exclude the unpublished tail.
Explicit snapshots MUST resolve exactly, not silently rebind to a later branch head.
Relation-level `as_of` MUST pin data and its decoding schema; whole-program historical execution is separately selected.
Database selectors MUST NOT replace wall-clock `now()`.
Format-3 tracked `.orna/` MUST contain only `database.orna` and `store`; required published system records MUST use the shared store.
`database.orna` MUST carry `repository_format: 3` and the stable database UUID; a separate `format.orna` is a legacy-format input, not another new-format authority.

Initialization MUST generate one UUIDv4, preserve existing source, and neither stage nor create a Git commit implicitly. Changing database identity requires an explicit fork-as-new-database migration.
Published checkpoint/allocator/runtime summaries MUST remain historical observations; checking them out MUST NOT rewind live fences, leases or non-rewindable allocators.
Caches, credentials, mounts, sessions, rejected edit drafts and unpublished changes MUST NOT be written into tracked `.orna/`.
Private state MUST use the per-worktree administrative path.
Unpublished accepted state MUST be authoritative and crash-durable under the declared failure model.
Derived caches MUST be disposable and keyed by source/schema/store/interface generations.
Private state MUST never be added to ordinary commits or included by a naive working-directory copy advertised as a complete export.
Local database use MUST work without devtools, a VFS mount, or `orna serve`.
The local CLI MUST be able to own embedded state in-process when no local writer exists.
Concurrent local commands MAY use private IPC to the single owner, not an obligatory public daemon.
Correctness MUST NOT depend on experimental unsynchronized multi-process SQLite/Turso access.
Clones and worktrees MUST have independent workspace/runtime identities; database UUID alone MUST NOT identify a writer.
Published synchronization MUST use Git commits/fetch/push/merge.
Non-fast-forward or concurrent writes MUST be explicit conflicts, not hidden cross-clone locks.
Independent clones MUST NOT claim exactly-once external ingestion without a connector-specific coordination or idempotency contract.
The local durable CWD MUST use embedded Turso/SQLite-compatible transaction storage, with no mandatory external server.
Row writes and associated checkpoint/request outcomes MUST commit atomically in the owning local transaction.
Implementations MUST document process/OS/power-loss guarantees, flush assumptions and measured settings.
There MUST be at most one owning writable embedded state instance per worktree under the single-owner profile.
Other local writers MUST coordinate with that owner or fail, never independently reopen an unsafe writable handle.
Ownership acquisition/recovery MUST fence old writers before admitting a replacement.
Git plumbing MAY use Git, gix or libgit2 while preserving native objects and observable Git semantics.
Every acknowledged row containing new content MUST have durable verified new objects and native retention roots; a hash string in SQLite is insufficient.
Inherited promised objects MAY remain unhydrated only with recorded snapshot/promisor evidence; newly imported unknown bytes MUST NOT be acknowledged as merely promised.
Runtime pin refs MUST be local, owner-scoped and excluded from ordinary remote push; export of unpublished work MUST first freeze a recoverable consistent root.
Recovery MUST distinguish unaccepted scratch, accepted pending content, and published content; cleanup MUST NOT infer orphanhood from one absent in-memory handle.
Disk-full, cancellation, source mutation and failed flush MUST leave no falsely acknowledged dependent row; uncertain external effects MUST remain explicitly uncertain.
Git GC/repack MUST share the declared maintenance boundary. Concurrent external destructive prune that bypasses protection is unsupported and MUST NOT be advertised as safe.
Creating a branch at HEAD MUST preserve CWD/index and create no implicit commit.
Selecting a branch at the same commit MUST preserve pending data, staged/unstaged source differences and non-rewindable continuity state.
A different-commit checkout MUST run CHECKOUT-3 with exact target validation, conflict preservation and recoverable state transitions.
Staging MUST bind the exact selected source/schema/row/content candidate and preserve unrelated staged or partially staged paths.
The index store MUST remain semantically complete and decode under its staged schema; missing dependencies or incompatible staged schemas MUST be rejected, not silently repaired using CWD.
Repeated staging MUST be deterministic and metadata-only staging MUST NOT hydrate media payloads.
Internal `.orna/store` paths MUST be managed atomically by Orna. Direct edits by other Git tools are detected as external candidate changes, not accepted without graph/schema validation.
A failed/stale checkout plan MUST leave current accepted state unchanged and preserve all drafts/unrelated changes.
Checkout recovery MUST inspect actual refs and journal progress; it MUST NOT force a ref back after another writer advances it.
A commit mount MUST be immutable; a branch-name snapshot mount MUST resolve once rather than move during reads.
A workspace mount MUST share the selected worktree's CWD, not create an untracked independent copy. Independent work requires another worktree/clone.
High-rate writes MUST become durable and queryable in embedded Turso before publication.
Status output MUST summarise pending high-rate changes rather than emit one path per pending row.

The default compact writer target is 16 MiB of compressed data, with an 8–32 MiB normal tuning range and the compact profile's 64 MiB file bound. An implementation MAY choose a target within that range but MUST expose the effective policy. A changed tuning value does not change logical rows or checkpoint meaning.
A maximum pending age MAY cause publication of a smaller complete batch; the profile default is 60 seconds.
Publication policy MUST NOT introduce a different table declaration kind.
Effective policy and pending/published state MUST be visible through `sys.Storage` and runtime maintenance metadata.
A publication commit MUST use a private tree/index built only from the captured base and frozen runtime batch. It MUST NOT commit unrelated human edits.

Before publication is reported complete, the ordinary index MUST be reconciled so it contains no accidental staged reversal of published managed paths, while preserving every unrelated staged change and staged/unstaged boundary.

Unresolved merges, rebases, overlapping managed-path edits or unreconcilable index state MUST pause automatic publication. Durable ingestion may continue within configured storage limits; exhaustion fails explicitly rather than discarding the tail.
Complete objects and their required durability barriers MUST precede a visible ref that names them.
Failure before ref advancement MUST preserve the pending batch. Unreferenced objects are permitted; a false successful publication result is not.
Failure after ref advancement MUST recover index/worktree reconciliation as well as Turso cleanup. Recognising the batch in the committed manifest is necessary but not sufficient.
A reader MUST observe the old snapshot plus the unpublished tail or the new snapshot with the published batch excluded from the tail. It MUST NOT observe duplicate or missing logical rows.
Ref updates MUST use expected-old-object compare-and-set and revalidate the selected branch/`HEAD` relationship. Concurrent commits MUST NOT be overwritten.

Recovery MUST preserve unrelated staged and unstaged changes. An index lock left by a crashed publisher may be removed only after owner-liveness and journal checks establish that it is that publisher's abandoned lock.
A normal Git commit made after completed publication MUST not reverse published managed data unless the user explicitly staged such a reversal.

Graceful writer shutdown SHOULD publish eligible batches after its children have terminated and open activations have reached a boundary. A pending publication conflict does not justify discarding the local tail.
Status MUST report remaining unpublished CWD changes.

Transferring resumable execution to another clone requires publishing and pushing the recoverable state, then fetching the resulting snapshot in the receiving clone. Loss of an unpublished local tail can be repaired only by replayable source data or an independently preserved copy of that tail.
Pending graph objects MUST be native-pinned before mutation acknowledgement and remain protected through publication/recovery.
Auto-publication MUST be opt-in; the initial product defaults to explicit publication so successful saves do not silently create Git commits.
`.orna/store` index reconciliation MUST preserve separately staged logical changes and never stage the reverse of an automatically published batch.
Published system-watermark rows MUST be folded with the same batch without turning historical data into current operational authority.
Every new-format table MUST have one ordered map from typed primary key to stored row value, bound to a stable table/schema identity.
Table lookup/order MUST use the language's logical key comparison, not filename order, CBOR byte order or hash order.
The canonical page/group algorithm, encoding and bounds MUST be those in ORP-1; runtime optimizations MUST produce identical canonical output for the same logical snapshot.
Blob fields MUST use small annotated-content references in stored rows; media bytes MUST never be expanded into row-page bytes or base64 row text.
Large rows/strings/collections MUST use the shared value-overflow graph so metadata pages and direct dependency fanout remain bounded.
Copy-on-write updates MUST reuse unchanged nodes where canonical boundaries permit it; changed indices and payload bytes MUST be measured separately.
Partial fetch MUST preserve exact schema/root pins and return unavailable rather than empty/successfully truncated results on missing objects.
Secondary indexes and long-key VFS name indexes MUST use the same ordered store profile and commit atomically with the rows they index.
An unindexed scan MAY require broad reads; explain/counters MUST distinguish estimated from actual transfer, decode and scan work.
Page rewrites/repacking/rechunking MUST NOT produce logical mutations when decoded values/annotations are unchanged.
Mutation/assertion/reference validation MUST be shared across all entrypoints; no VFS-specific weaker rules are permitted.
Raw storage nodes MUST not be exposed as writable row files; external graph modification requires full admission before use.
Format-1/2 histories MUST retain versioned readers. Migration MUST NOT dual-write the old row layouts or silently upgrade a historical commit.
New `sys.Storage` metadata MUST describe root, schema, generation, row count when known, and observed bytes/availability; removed preference/placement modes MUST NOT survive as hidden toggles.
The native graph MUST connect all direct dependencies through real Git tree entries, use one object store, and reject mismatching, unused or type-invalid dependency edges.
A committed snapshot MUST identify all required local source, rows and content through native Git reachability and all dependencies through exact gitlinks/recorded origins.
Partial clones MAY defer blob payloads using ordinary filters and promisor remotes; unknown missing objects MUST be distinguished from promised objects.
A successful full/offline export MUST include all selected snapshot closure and recursive pinned dependencies, not just a pointer-only clone or mounted text files.
Fetch/push/clone MUST preserve Git compatibility and never require LFS to retrieve required content.
Sparse checkout MUST control materialized paths only; it MUST NOT be presented as an availability or confidentiality boundary.
Metadata-only queries and updates MUST read zero media payload bytes; metadata objects and tree traffic MUST be accounted separately.
A full mirror of the superproject is not a complete submodule copy; export verification MUST recursively account for dependency object databases.
Refs required for allocator/consumer continuity MUST be synchronized with their existing ordering/validation rules; private edit/capture pins MUST NOT be exposed by ordinary push.
Git host size/push/object limits MUST be reported as deployment constraints. Native format compatibility MUST NOT be advertised as unlimited GitHub storage.
Collection MUST preserve content reachable from retained commits, local pins, pending accepted changes, open pins and unfinished recovery journals.
Repository clone credentials MUST be treated as access to repository content; VFS path hiding, namespaces or filtered clone are not row-level permissions.
Offline failure MUST name unavailable scope without exposing secrets; it MUST NOT silently use a current host file or another snapshot.
Stable table/field identities MUST survive supported renames; a textual name match alone MUST NOT establish continuity.
Schema changes MUST be admitted against affected rows, references, assertions, indexes and stored codecs before visibility.
Historical rows MUST be decoded under their historical schema/value profile; current source MUST NOT silently reinterpret them.
Semantic diff MUST compare logical fields and Blob annotations/content, not storage page or Git-layout IDs.
A three-way merge MUST validate the merged program/schema/data/content closure and constraints before publishing; a conflict-free Git text merge is not sufficient.

Conflicting replacements of one Blob MUST be reported as value conflicts unless an explicit application merge function supplies a validated replacement; concatenating chunk lists is not a default merge.
Explicit rekey MUST use normal immutable-key/reference rules and emit one logical rekey with old/new address, not a filename guess.
A representation-only rewrite MUST preserve semantic rows and content commitments. Defaulting new annotations in migration is an explicit semantic migration, not falsely an empty semantic diff.
Required introduction defaults/fallbacks MUST be frozen under the source/schema revision rather than reevaluated on every historical read.
A failed migration/merge/checkout MUST preserve accepted state and conflicting user edits; no automatic ref reset, inferred winner or unknown-schema overwrite is allowed.
Local commands trust the invoking OS user. Orna v1 does not define principals, groups, grants, row ACLs, device roles or an enterprise policy language.
`orna serve` binds to loopback by default. Remote deployment SHOULD use normal SSH, Tailscale, or a trusted authenticated reverse proxy/TLS boundary.
Public anonymous mutation or arbitrary remote REPL execution is outside the trusted v1 profile.
Orna MUST NOT require a separate handwritten permissions/package manifest merely to restate a component's WIT imports and exports.
WIT imports/exports and the pinned Git object identify the portable interface and code. Installing/running the extension is the trust decision.
A Wasm extension MUST NOT receive raw pointers/handles to Turso or Git internals. Host calls use typed interfaces so a trap cannot corrupt repository/runtime memory.
Implementations SHOULD enforce coarse execution budgets and cancellation for portable components. These controls bound execution; they do not grant per-device permissions.
Native extensions run with the host process's trust and MUST be labeled as such. Orna does not sandbox native extensions.
Orna MUST NOT commit plaintext secret values by default.
Secret values MUST be redacted from Inspect, Display, Present, diagnostics, traces and `sys` unless an explicitly privileged operation requests disclosure.
An SOPS provider MUST decrypt in memory and SHOULD avoid writing plaintext temporary files.
A clone without the decryption identity MUST remain able to inspect committed non-secret data and MUST report dependent runs as unavailable rather than corrupt.
A `SecretRef` may be displayed and serialized by stable name; the resolved secret value may not.
`sys.Secret` MUST expose metadata such as name, provider and availability but MUST NOT expose secret contents.
`orna serve` provides Git transport, page/query endpoints and WebSocket presentation deltas for its clone.
`orna serve` MUST NOT automatically invoke root `main()` or unrelated stream programs.
A different clone running `orna serve` serves that clone's HEAD and CWD; CWD MUST remain local to that clone.
The default listener MUST bind only to loopback unless the operator explicitly selects another address.
Core Orna does not define principals, groups, grants, per-device roles or row-level permissions.
Binding beyond loopback MUST be explicit and MUST produce a clear status indication of the exposed interfaces.
Git transport MUST remain usable when the optional Git/database web frontend is absent.

The default frontend SHOULD be an ordinary, removable devtools application. An upstream `std.devtools` package or a vendored `devtools` module is permitted; neither name is privileged. The minimal source-hosted profile and exact source/resource ownership are defined in [source-hosted applications](#source-apps).
When installed as `/`, the default frontend SHOULD lead with database tables and also expose files, commits, branches, functions, dependencies, storage and runtime state.

Each canonical encoder MUST use the exact selected profile. OVB-1 legacy/wire encodings remain unchanged; OVB-2 uses the additions below. Strict decoders MUST reject aliases and foreign-profile tags before identity use.

A CWD reference MUST identify its captured generation. A context-free `[0]` is invalid. A decoder unable to resolve a pin MUST report `sys.snapshot.expired` or `sys.snapshot.incomplete`; it MUST NOT rebind the reference to current CWD.
A referenced database, type, table and key schema MUST agree. Decoding data from another snapshot does not implicitly import its schema or replace the current execution context.

Canonical text decoding MUST be type-directed and non-executable. It MUST distinguish optional absence, scalar values, row references and nominal construction according to the supplied schema, and validate all refinements before returning a value.
New annotated Blob values MUST preserve annotations through OVB-2 and MUST NOT silently lose them on old wire/export interfaces.
Stored and semantic reference tags MUST be rejected outside their recorded ROV-3/SOV-3 contexts; a raw SHA or Git OID is never permission to read content.

An implementation MUST decode and validate the complete message, required fields, canonical forms and configured limits before admitting its operation. It MUST reject duplicate map keys and noncanonical integer/length forms; it MUST NOT execute a partially decoded request.

Session resumption MUST preserve request reservations and terminal outcomes for that session while its lease remains valid. A new runtime generation MUST invalidate operational handles from the old generation. Durable request recovery may report old outcomes as data without reviving old handles or owners.

The client MUST apply the ordered operations to a temporary tree and publish them atomically only if its current revision equals the declared base and every operation succeeds. Otherwise it MUST discard the patch and request resynchronisation. It MUST NOT leave a partially patched visible tree.

A durable admission reservation and a terminal transactional claim are distinct records/states. The terminal claim and successful Orna writes MUST share one transaction. A reservation without a terminal claim MUST NOT be treated as permission to execute a potentially effectful request again.
Blob MUST represent a finite octet sequence with canonical media type and optional suffix hint. The metadata MUST NOT alter the raw-byte content commitment.
This release MUST NOT add intrinsic `File`, `Asset`, `Bytes` or `Clob` synonyms or mandatory tables. Existing `sys.File` source-catalogue objects remain distinct from media values.
Blob MUST work in ordinary stored/nested values; Blob primary keys remain inadmissible.
Content identity MUST be `(length, SHA256(raw bytes))`, independent of MIME, suffix, Git object header/algorithm, compression, chunking, path and snapshot.

Blob value equality MUST compare canonical annotations and exact content. `same_content` ignores annotations. Equal digests MUST NOT override detected unequal bytes; independently supplied equal-digest content without a shared admitted witness requires exact streamed comparison or explicit unavailability.
Detected content collisions MUST fail without overwriting or aliasing an existing content identity.

Loading a row, passing a same-database Blob reference, showing metadata, reading length/digest or changing MIME/title MUST NOT hydrate media just to form a `Vec<u8>`, encode a row or calculate its semantic digest.
Held values MUST retain their exact resolution context for their owner/pin lifetime; unavailable/expired values MUST NOT rebind through a later row or HEAD.
Structured portable annotated values MUST use negotiated OVB-2; old OVB-1 keeps its original bytes-only semantics. No implicit annotation-dropping or reference-in-byte-slot conversion is allowed.
Inspectors MUST display type, length, declaration and content commitment without payload dumps or remote analysis. The VFS/row representation MUST use small references, not base64 media.
`read` MUST check nonnegative offsets/lengths, offset at/before EOF, checked arithmetic and at most 8 MiB per call; only known EOF clips a successful result.
Range acquisition MUST fetch required descriptors/intersecting chunks and only separately bounded read-ahead. Whole Git-object overfetch MUST be measured, not called exact range transfer.
BlobWriter MUST be owner/runtime-bound and nonserializable, with open/finished/aborted states, serialized append/finish/abort, idempotent terminal outcomes and cancellation cleanup.
Begin/append/finish MUST enforce declared expected length, total quota and the format maximum 2^63−1. No unbounded buffer or temporary-file bypass is allowed.
Exact snapshot hydration MUST respect offline/network policy and cancellation; host `capture_file` is external I/O and remains forbidden in historical/pure/presenter/assertion contexts.
Format-3 row/argument/consumer semantic commitments MUST use the versioned SOV-3 domains, not Git layout OIDs or eager full-byte encodings.
Cross-format comparison MUST compare decoded values under explicit migration semantics, not unrelated digest bytes.

The existing live protocol MUST reject unnegotiated OVB-2/storage tags. Use typed safe inspector/reference responses and separately authorized content I/O, not automatic full-Blob result serialization.
Copying into an independent database MUST establish and protect destination closure before acknowledging a dependent row, with no hidden dependency on the original user's path.
Generic slicing/concatenation MUST produce octet-stream/null annotations unless it is an exact identity no-op; part of a JPEG does not automatically remain image/jpeg.
Byte export MUST mean original raw bytes. Full annotated value export MUST preserve metadata explicitly; an export operation cannot silently switch between these two promises.
Each nonterminal node MUST be an ordinary Git tree with `data` and optional `refs`; `data` is one canonical bounded CBOR blob and `refs` maps native OID names to exact child object types.
The direct dependency inventory in decoded data MUST exactly match `refs`, deduplicated by OID; missing, unused, malformed or wrong-type edges MUST be rejected.
Terminal binary chunks MUST be raw Git blobs. No separate media server, pointer-only object or second hash warehouse is permitted.
Node metadata MUST be at most 64 KiB and direct fanout at most 256; larger values/indices MUST use the same bounded graph recursively.
Objects MUST be validated under their format, schema and context before use. A shared child MUST NOT bypass per-parent semantic constraints.
Git SHA-1 and SHA-256 modes MUST retain native OID widths and verification; neither native OID equals the raw-content SHA-256 by definition.
The store root MUST contain only snapshot-required reachable state. Retained history belongs to ancestry/pins, not a current-root catalogue of every historical object.
The root Blob descriptor MUST bind exact length, raw-byte SHA-256 and its native content graph. MIME and suffix MUST be stored with each referencing value, not as global facts about a hash.
Chunk entries MUST bind native object OID, byte length and independent chunk SHA-256; offset traversal MUST validate lengths, height and bounds.
Zero-length content MUST have one canonical empty descriptor; zero-length nonempty-index children, wrong total length and excessive height MUST be rejected.
Metadata-only access MUST not read chunks. Full verification MUST compare every chunk plus the complete raw-content digest before claiming full integrity.
The chosen partition rule MUST be reproducible; insertions and adversarial patterns MUST have explicit bounded-resource behaviour and measured index churn.
Native Git graph validation MUST not be replaced by checking a descriptor string. Missing promised data is unavailable; unknown missing data is corruption/incomplete closure.
All newly persisted Blob fields MUST use reference form regardless of payload size. Small Blobs may use one terminal chunk, not a second inline-row mode.
Cross-representation equality and semantic diff MUST ignore rechunking, graph OIDs and Git repacking while retaining annotation changes.

Import MUST capture the actual bytes, not a mutable source path or URL. Once the row commit is acknowledged, removing the source MUST NOT invalidate the imported Blob. Import MUST NOT automatically create a global media catalogue or unrelated derived records.

File capture MUST require an authorised root and a safe relative path, resolve beneath the held root without traversal/symlink races, reject device/FIFO/socket/directory inputs, enforce the byte bound, and avoid implicit shell construction. Missing permission, changed source, quota exhaustion and cancellation MUST have distinct typed outcomes without leaking private path details.

A regular-file capture MUST compare identity, size and modification observations before/after the streamed read and reject detected changes as `sys.blob.source_changed`. Without an OS snapshot or cooperating source lock it guarantees the exact observed byte stream, not an atomic historical photograph of a concurrently modified external file. Stronger source-snapshot claims require the relevant lock/snapshot witness.

Long byte acquisition MUST NOT hold an exclusive database write lock or one open SQLite transaction for its duration. Its immutable result is installed through the existing optimistic/activation boundary. On conflict, Orna-controlled changes roll back; external reading is not undone. A retry uses the captured protected Blob where valid, not an unnoticed reread of a newer source.

Programmatic/network ingestion MUST use the same owned Blob writer and atomic row/dependency boundary as regular-file import. Adapter staging is local temporary state, not another persistent content service. Quotas MUST include quarantined, protected, pending and retained objects as separate observable categories.

Duplicate ingestion of identical bytes MAY share payload storage, but MUST NOT silently merge two distinct application rows or import events. Row deduplication follows the application's keys and transaction rules; content deduplication follows raw-byte identity, regardless of media annotations; annotated value equality remains separate.

Default inspection MUST make Blob length and content identity available without a plugin or payload read. Common-format inspection SHOULD be supplied by bundled, version-pinned ordinary library functions, not require a separately administered extraction service. An unknown format remains storable, queryable by record metadata and retrievable.

A decoder MUST consume the selected immutable Blob through bounded reads, not reopen its import pathname. Its output MUST distinguish valid properties, absent embedded properties, unsupported formats, malformed content and resource/unavailable failures. File extensions and supplied MIME strings MUST NOT substitute for byte validation.

Decoding/sniffing MUST be side-effect-free with respect to database state; recording its results is an explicit ordinary transaction. Inspecting a Blob MUST NOT silently start network analysis, purchase inference, run embedded scripts/macros, execute source contained in a document or persist a catalogue of guesses.

A decoded property's cache key MUST bind content identity, decoder code/dependency revision, output schema and effective options/bounds that affect the result. A partial result obtained under a small budget MUST NOT masquerade as the complete result under another budget. Cache data belongs in local runtime/cache storage; it MUST NOT be required to interpret a committed record.

Native libraries and explicitly authorised decoder processes MAY implement codecs behind typed operations. They MUST use bounded time/memory/output, cancellation, argument-vector execution and protected temporary resources. Their presence MUST NOT create a separate file catalogue or bypass transaction, source-pin and privacy rules.

A persisted analysis result MUST identify every input revision that affects it, function/dependency revision, provider/model coordinate, effective parameters/prompt, output schema, time and success/failure/uncertainty state. Source-byte identity alone is insufficient when related notes, prior outputs or external context participate.

Persisted annotations/results MUST be ordinary typed records related to their inputs. User corrections and original bytes MUST be preserved independently of regenerated results. Re-analysis MUST NOT silently replace historical observations or mutate an older snapshot.

External model use, disclosure of content and nontrivial cost MUST require explicit host/operator policy. Recorded provenance does not guarantee a changing external service can reproduce the result. Reproducibility MUST distinguish retained output replay from re-execution with retained model artifacts.

Historical evaluation MUST use the selected program/data/result revisions. It MUST NOT silently run the host's newest decoder/model to fill a missing historical property. Explicit new analysis of old immutable content is a new operation with a new result, not a revision of history.
Devtools MUST be ordinary selected Orna source, not a privileged native Git homepage or separate playground product.
Browse and console results MUST use shared typed inspection. Run MUST call the real parser/resolver/evaluator; simulated results are not completion.
Portable UI meaning MUST not depend on HTML, CSS or DOM. The web renderer SHOULD use native semantic controls and absent/minimal optional CSS.
The selected application source/resources MUST be the actual executed inputs; removal MUST not trigger hidden reinstallation or native fallback.
Pinned `std` submodules MUST retain normal Git semantics. Editing a dependency requires its own commit then a parent gitlink update, or an explicit local vendor/fork; no silent mutable overlay.
CSS, browser host bindings and Wasm outputs MUST belong to renderer-package resources or ordinary Blob fields. No compulsory File/Asset registry or `std.devtools.Asset` primitive is permitted.
Package resources MUST resolve in the caller's admitted dependency/source snapshot. Host paths, newest installed libraries and mutable remote URLs cannot replace those inputs silently.
Builds MUST bind source, dependencies, resources, toolchain and host ABI coherently; offline claims require complete dependency closure.
Source-hosted conformance MUST put routing, HTML generation, asset serving and application orchestration in replaceable Orna code; a wrapper around a complete native server fails this claim.
CLI serving MUST invoke only the selected serving entry and retain loopback/trusted-perimeter defaults; full Server conformance still requires the existing exact protocol endpoints.
Each mutation MUST use shared short activation/request transactions; listeners and browser waits are supervised lifetimes, not open database transactions.

The first web implementation MAY use request/response HTML and forms. It MUST bound input, enforce origin/CSRF/session checks, and never blindly replay an uncertain mutation. This is not a full live-protocol claim.
Blob summaries MUST be metadata-only. Explicit media/content responses MUST check authority and snapshot identity; inspection of HTML/SVG/JS MUST not execute it.
Media responses SHOULD support RFC 9110 HEAD, single byte ranges and immutable validators through the shared Blob reader, with correct 206/416 and truncated-stream failure behaviour.

The later browser profile MUST run protocol/control/rendering code authored in Orna through a Wasm build of the shared evaluator initially; a direct compiler may replace it with equivalent semantics later.
Generated JS MAY bind browser APIs only; no app-specific Git/table logic or second Orna language implementation. Server handles/closures MUST NOT become client authority.
Page updates MUST use explicit immutable-model transitions. The console's scratch bindings MUST NOT overwrite the page's pinned application environment.
Focus/caret/unsent drafts/local feedback MUST remain responsive and not be overwritten by unrelated server results.
Connection resume, durable request recovery and page-state restoration MUST be separate promises; expired sessions MUST NOT replay mutation transcripts.
Source/runtime upgrades MUST switch coherent generations for new sessions; old actions MUST NOT silently acquire new meanings. Invalid app source MUST leave local core recovery usable.
Replaceability MUST be demonstrated by a second ordinary application and an independent minimal Orna renderer/HTTP composition using only public interfaces.
The minimum demonstration MUST use actual row/Blob storage: import, query, retrieve/play, metadata edit, historical read and complete offline reopen. A mock HTML page is not engine evidence.
A virtual row directory MUST address database/table/typed key; `data.orna` MUST encode stored non-key fields only, under that snapshot's schema.
Virtual row text and sibling content files MUST be projections of the shared row store, not materialized competing authoritative copies.
Unchanged schema-directed Blob references MUST resolve internally in the captured row/draft context without reopening the mount or reading payloads.
Relative paths MUST stay within that field's registered projection. Absolute paths, symlink/traversal escapes and implicit cross-row references MUST fail.
Commit selectors MUST pin one snapshot; a branch-name snapshot selector resolves once. Workspace mounts MUST share one selected worktree's durable CWD.
Every accepted edit MUST use normal transaction/assertion/reference/permission validation and never automatically create a Git commit.
FUSE `release` MUST NOT be the only rejection/durability point; callback behavior and close-error limitations MUST be disclosed.
Dirty sequence capture and acceptance MUST serialize with writes; `dup`/fork/repeated flush MUST not create a second acceptance of the same candidate.
Invalid/stale candidates MUST preserve original accepted values, protect retained draft bytes and return a stable error/diagnostic association.
A metadata-only save MUST not fetch or rehash sibling content. A binary save MAY require streaming the entire resulting bytes to establish its raw SHA-256; memory remains bounded.
Normal save CAS MUST compare the captured write/temp-create baseline. Strong initial-read protection MUST be claimed only for a retained edit token/guarded operation.
Renaming a suffix MUST not transcode bytes, rename columns or rekey a row. Compatible aliases update only the explicit suffix hint through CAS.
Removing a required Blob MUST fail; optional Blob unlink MAY set that field to null after validation. Deleting `data.orna` MUST fail; row deletion is an explicit database operation.
Hard links, device nodes, symlinks and writable shared mmap are unsupported in VFS-1 and MUST fail explicitly. Private mmap/read copies do not modify the database.
Multiple file saves MUST NOT be guessed into one transaction. `orna edit --row PATH` provides explicit grouped row/content admission; separate updates may reject cross-field constraints.
Reserved/colliding names MUST be escaped reversibly, not rejected as otherwise valid database keys or merged by case-folding.
Directory iteration MUST be lazy/paged and pinned; lookup of a known key MUST use the index. An exhaustive recursive scan can still fetch all requested data.
`stat`, directory listings and row documents MUST not sniff/decode/download Blob content; raw-file size comes from the exact content descriptor.
Schema changes, MIME path changes and API writes MUST invalidate directory/attribute caches coherently. Existing handles MUST not retarget to a different row or reordered collection element.

Source files MAY be edited through the shared workspace source path; complete candidate validation and explicit grouped source edits are required when several files change together. No evaluation occurs during speculative file writes.
Sync/rename acknowledgement, new content pins, local row commitment and namespace recovery MUST be journalled so crashes cannot lose acknowledged content.
FUSE writeback caching MUST be off initially; supported caching/IO modes MUST preserve per-open generation semantics despite non-VFS database writers.
The adapter MUST NOT expose a fake `.git` directory or writable raw store. Git commands target the backing repository, never generated row documents.
Unmount MUST refuse dirty/unresolved accepted-state recovery unless an explicit policy retains it safely. It MUST NOT report discarded drafts as saved.
Every new Blob MUST have a valid concrete declared MIME value; constructors without knowledge use application/octet-stream, never a wildcard or empty string.

Normalization MUST lowercase type/subtype/parameter names, sort parameters, normalize charset case, and preserve other case-sensitive parameter values; duplicate names, controls and malformed quoted strings MUST fail.
A preferred suffix MUST be chosen from MIME-1 by essence; a compatible explicit safe hint overrides it, otherwise unknown types use bin.
Explicit hints MUST be lowercase safe ASCII suffix segments of at most 32 bytes, without leading dot, slash, backslash, empty segments or traversal. Known-type incompatible hints MUST fail.
Defaults matching the preferred suffix MUST canonicalize to no hint; normal spelling/quoting/case variations MUST not create different annotated values.

Import resolution MUST be explicit declaration first, then bounded trusted detection, then a uniquely mapped suffix, then octet-stream. Conflicting observations MUST be disclosed; host-specific MIME registries cannot silently decide persistent metadata.
Detection MUST NOT run on listings/stat/metadata-only edits. Unsupported or damaged content MUST remain preservable unless an explicit schema constraint requires a valid format.
MIME changes MUST update projected filenames atomically while keeping existing content handles pinned. Renames do not transcode or grant executable status.
HTML/SVG/JS previews MUST not execute merely because the stored declaration requests it. Trusted application assets and arbitrary user-content downloads require different explicit serving policies.
Implementations MUST dispatch readers by recorded repository/value formats, not the CLI version or the current host's defaults.
Existing format-1/2 commits MUST remain immutable and readable under their original decoders and equality/digest semantics.
New-format writes MUST use one canonical row store; loose/compact/hybrid dual-writing is forbidden.
Legacy Blob annotation defaults MUST be explicit: octet-stream and no suffix, without downloading or decoding every payload during metadata migration.
Annotation migration MUST be reported as a semantic profile transition; preservation of raw bytes is not proof of unchanged annotated value identity.
A migration failure MUST preserve the old authoritative snapshot/tail and all user edits; it MUST NOT partially change the active writer.
Source and API changes MUST be atomic with the format transition; removed storage-preference APIs MUST not secretly choose legacy layouts.
Consumers with Blob-containing arguments MUST not reset progress because the argument encoding domain changed; require an explicit validated migration map or fail closed.
New protocols MUST explicitly negotiate new value codecs; old live endpoints and fingerprints MUST remain byte-for-byte legacy-compatible for their admitted values.
Unsupported annotated values on legacy wire MUST fail before effects or use the specified retained-without-value result after an already committed operation. No implicit downcast to bytes.
Every valid language fixture requires successful parse, name resolution and type checking. Parser-only success MUST NOT be presented as full validity.
Every invalid fixture identifies the expected failing phase and stable diagnostic code.

The reference `examples/reference/` project is loaded as one complete database project: parse reachable modules, resolve/type-check them with its declared intrinsic environment and supplied modules, admit every provided legacy row fixture through its declared input context, reconstruct its typed key and validate fields/units before importing it into the current row engine. Do not silently reinterpret fixture paths as format-3 storage.

Bundle validation distinguishes: a test is specified, a test exists in an implementation, and a test passed. Document/index checks MUST NOT claim that Orna source executed when no implementation was run.

The corpus covers each normative syntax alternative, precedence boundary and deliberately invalid ambiguous form. It need not manufacture a positive and negative file for every mechanical EBNF helper production.

A generated requirement-to-test coverage report SHOULD expose untested normative behaviour, but it MUST remain a reporting layer over ordinary tests rather than a new test language or CI system. Informative rationale is excluded from the denominator.

`tests/conformance-manifest.json` MUST index valid, invalid and complete-project fixtures. A complete-project fixture MUST include `load_rows`, which admits the supplied fixture rows through their declared legacy input reader, validates them against the resolved schema/units, then imports them into the current row engine; fixture files do not enable a second new-format row writer.

`tests/requirement-evidence.json` MUST attach a non-empty `tests` list to every numbered requirement. Entries may name ordinary source fixtures, project fixtures, vector suites, behavioural/fault scenarios, interoperability suites, benchmark suites or an explicit inspection requirement. The mapping is a test plan, not evidence that an implementation has executed it.

Machine-testable normative behaviour MUST be identified as requiring an executable fixture, vector, project, scenario or implementation suite. A plan without an implemented test remains unexecuted. Bundle validation MUST fail when a requirement has no recorded evidence obligation; production conformance additionally requires the applicable implementation evidence to pass.
Test tooling SHOULD support temporary branch/worktree isolation without requiring a separately administered test server.
Branch-based tests MUST NOT imply that mocks or conventional unit tests are forbidden; the branch model is an integration-state primitive, not a ban on other testing methods.
A release report MUST distinguish authored conformance cases from executed implementation evidence and MUST NOT infer a pass from a filename, requirement association, file count or manifest validity.

A complete example project MUST include every required module/schema or pin an available dependency with an exact interface. Placeholder connector attachment points do not make an example self-contained.

Benchmark, cross-platform, interoperability, security and fault obligations determine an implementation's evidence for its claimed profile. They MUST NOT be used as permission to choose different observable semantics.

Features outside the declared language/profile are absent, not implicitly implementation-defined. A source program relying on such a feature MUST receive an unsupported-feature or resolution diagnostic rather than silently acquiring vendor-specific behaviour under the same portable coordinate.
Removal of postfix `?`, replacement of a function return arrow, and `var` to `let` are mechanical only when token-aware parsing proves the context.
A tool MUST NOT rewrite anonymous-function `=>` while migrating case arms.
